body.translated_text: <s>Kṣemendra</s>: <s>Narmamālā</s>
The First Jest

children.text: yenedaṃ svecchayā sarvaṃ māyayā mohitaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: He by whom this entire world is deluded through <s>māyā</s> (illusion) at his own will,

children.text: sa jayatyajitaḥ śrīmān kāyasthaḥ parameśvaraḥ // KNarm_1.1 //
children.translated_text: that unconquered, glorious <s>Kāyastha</s> (scribe), the supreme lord, is victorious! // KNarm_1.1 //
There exists, foremost among the fortunate, adorned by circles of the learned,
the realm of <s>Kaśmīra</s>, whose pride surpasses even the abode of undivided <s>Indra</s> // KNarm_1.2 //
In which, having restrained the enemies' valor with the pillars of his mighty arms,
the glorious King <s>Ananta</s>, conqueror of tribute-bearers, reigns like <s>Trivikrama</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) // KNarm_1.3 //
By that discerning one, when afflictions upon the people had been warded off,
the corrupt officials ... were reduced to mere memory // KNarm_1.4 //
By a certain crest-jewel among the witty, playful in disposition,
most distinguished in the assembly of scholars, a certain sympathetic person // KNarm_1.5 //
was urged to compose the tale of past <s>Kāyastha</s> conduct for the sake of laughter;
and in that connection, he creates a mockery of wicked conduct // KNarm_1.6 //
Obeisance to the ordainer of <s>māyā</s> (illusion), who created the world's manifold display,
to <s>Purahārin</s> (the destroyer of cities), who effects creation, maintenance, and dissolution // KNarm_1.7 //
To the all-pervading, birthless, quality-less one who bears the arts (<s>kalā</s>),
to you, the superintendent of all, the consumer of all poison (<s>kālakūṭa</s>) // KNarm_1.8 //
Long ago, when the <s>Daityas</s> (demons) were slain by the mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
their household accountant, grieving and filled with lasting dispassion, // KNarm_1.9 //
going to the bank of the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> (river of hell), performed austerities for a thousand years,
subsisting on his own urine as drink, out of enmity toward the gods // KNarm_1.10 //
Pleased, <s>Kali</s> himself, the boon-giver, approached him and spoke:
'Go, my child, to the earth, for the destruction of all gods!' // KNarm_1.11 //
'With this weapon of the pen (<s>kalama</s>), given by me, which strikes,
you shall render the gods cut off from lamp-offerings and flowers, devoid of incense, stripped bare, // KNarm_1.12 //
fallen from their temples, smeared with dust, crying "Alas!", surrounded by dogs;
you shall make all the gods into beggars craving food and water // KNarm_1.13 //

children.text: jagati brāhmaṇānāṃ ca vṛtticchede tvayā kṛte /
children.translated_text: 'When you have cut off the livelihood of the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in the world,

children.text: yajñacchedādvinaṅkṣyanti divi devā na saṃśayaḥ // KNarm_1.14 //
children.translated_text: the gods in heaven shall perish from the cessation of sacrifices—without doubt // KNarm_1.14 //
'Since you wept in heaven when the destruction of the <s>Daityas</s> was accomplished,

children.text: tasmāttvaṃ diviro nāma bhuvi khyāto bhaviṣyasi // KNarm_1.15 //
children.translated_text: therefore you shall be known on earth by the name <s>Divira</s> (one who wept in heaven) // KNarm_1.15 //
'He whose ink (<s>maṣī</s>) is all-dark, whose <s>Kālī</s> (ink-pot) has swallowed everything,
whose pen is always entirely of iron—it shall grant him the accomplishment of all aims // KNarm_1.16 //
'In your lineage here shall be born <s>Daityas</s> in the form of <s>Diviras</s> (scribes),

children.text: yairiyaṃ labdhavibhavaiḥ pṛthivī na bhaviṣyati // KNarm_1.17 //
children.translated_text: by whom, having gained power, this earth shall cease to exist' // KNarm_1.17 //
Having said this, when <s>Kali</s> disappeared, that evil-minded one,

children.text: yāti kāle suvipule mahīmavatatāra saḥ // KNarm_1.18 //
children.translated_text: when a vast span of time had passed, descended to the earth // KNarm_1.18 //
Then, born on earth from a butcher (<s>saunika</s>), a striker of vital spots,
from the wife of a <s>kuddālika</s> (digger), he whose vow was the uprooting of the world // KNarm_1.19 //
By the fierce ones born in his lineage, robbers of all livelihoods,
harsh, friends to none, sinful, seizers of everything, // KNarm_1.20 //
like world-endings devouring all things movable and immovable everywhere,
their entire bodies smeared with ink, as if embraced by <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death), // KNarm_1.21 //
going down softly, then suddenly rising up stiffly,
like excrement—these <s>Kāyasthas</s>, doers of harm, // KNarm_1.22 //
many-faced during service, greedy, many-armed,
of many tricks in deception, many-formed enemies of the gods— // KNarm_1.23 //
when cities, villages, towns, and settlements were pervaded [by them],
at that time, scratching the sky with his ink-smeared pen, // KNarm_1.24 //
<s>Kali</s> danced, with scissors in hand, cloaked in birch-bark;
'This great <s>Asura</s> (demon), called "Bellows-girded," all-devouring,
is born for the destruction of the world!'—so declared the hosts of <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls) // KNarm_1.25 //
By that robber of the gods' property, cutter of cattle-feed and salt,

children.text: bhujyate pīyate bhūri divireṇa divāniśam // KNarm_1.26 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Divira</s> (scribe) consumes and drinks abundantly, day and night // KNarm_1.26 //
When Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> formerly strode across the three worlds with devotion,

children.text: dharmaḥ prayāto dravatāṃ maṣīrūpeṇa tiṣṭhati // KNarm_1.27 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), having turned to liquid, remains in the form of ink // KNarm_1.27 //
The destroyer of the daily and occasional rites of gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, and men—
when that lord of the <s>Kāyasthas</s> again strides across the three worlds, // KNarm_1.28 //
<s>Kali</s>, having turned to liquid, remains in the form of ink;

children.text: yathā svargapradā gaṅgā tathaiṣā narakapradā // KNarm_1.29 //
children.translated_text: just as <s>Gaṅgā</s> grants heaven, so this [ink] grants hell // KNarm_1.29 //
Afflicted by notorious villages, chains, and clubs,
he, having attained dispassion out of fear, became a great ascetic // KNarm_1.30 //
Then, his affliction broken, abandoning his vow, he went to distant lands;
forgotten with time, returning as one skilled in birch-bark [documents], feigning desirelessness, // KNarm_1.31 //
gradually through village appointment, then in the city, as chief accountant,
honored through hypocrisy, he obtained the office of household steward by fate's decree // KNarm_1.32 //
By his cruel dependents, who lived by sycophancy,
the earth was made devoid of wealth by these brazen thieves // KNarm_1.33 //
<s>Dambhadhvaja</s> (Hypocrisy-banner), <s>Niṣprapañca</s> (Guileless-seeming), <s>Lubdhaka</s> (Greedy), <s>Kalamākara</s> (Pen-mine),
<s>Sūcīmukha</s> (Needle-face), <s>Bhūrjagupta</s> (Birch-bark-hidden), and <s>Mahīmaṇḍa</s> (Earth-circle)—these were unbearable; // KNarm_1.34 //
these seven incarnations of <s>Daityas</s> (demons), officials by virtue of his glory,

children.text: luṇṭhyā vadhyāśca pūjyā ye sarva ityavadanmadāt // KNarm_1.35 //
children.translated_text: who arrogantly declared: 'All—whether to be plundered or punished—are to be worshipped [i.e., fleeced]' // KNarm_1.35 //
<s>Upatāpa</s> (Affliction), <s>Vajrapāta</s> (Thunderbolt-fall), <s>Parigha</s> (Iron-bar), <s>Dvārabhañjaka</s> (Door-breaker),
<s>Dhūmaketu</s> (Comet), <s>Kapimukha</s> (Monkey-face), <s>Kukṣibheda</s> (Belly-splitter), <s>Gṛholmuka</s> (House-firebrand)— // KNarm_1.36 //
these eight <s>Piśācas</s> (ghouls) were his foremost soldiers, his advance guard,
who roamed about with staffs in hand for the destruction of the mortal world // KNarm_1.37 //
He, surrounded by hundreds of servants, always in the worship of <s>Dambhahara</s> (the god of hypocrisy),
recites a hymn, crying 'Hā! Hā!' with tearful eyes: // KNarm_1.38 //
[With a sweet, captivating voice, seen by the onlooking audience:]

children.text: hyaḥ kiyanto mayā dattāḥ prāyasthā vijayeśvare // KNarm_1.39 //
children.translated_text: 'How many were assigned by me yesterday as death-dues at <s>Vijayeśvara</s>?' // KNarm_1.39 //
'Victorious is <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord), whose infinite glory is resplendent!'
'Let these seventy-three be placed above those stationed first!' // KNarm_1.40 //
'He who is replete with the wealth of glory, compassion, knowledge, and supreme bliss—'

children.text: prāyasthāne mṛtā bhaṭṭāḥ kṛṣyantāṃ gulphadāmabhiḥ // KNarm_1.41 //
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhaṭṭas</s> who died at the <s>prāyasthāna</s> (death-dues station), let them be dragged by ankle-ropes!' // KNarm_1.41 //
'He whose greatness is illuminated by knowledge, that undefeated one, is victorious!'
'Let the officials who produce smokeless smoke go to the villages!' // KNarm_1.42 //
'To the one whose form is all bliss, the cause of all auspiciousness—'
'Having confiscated everything, those who obstruct punishment are to be executed!' // KNarm_1.43 //
'Obeisance to <s>Brahman</s> whose form is consciousness, who removes all afflictions!'
'The people, when squeezed, exude [wealth] just like <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) seeds!' // KNarm_1.44 //
Thus, loud with such hymns and the like, deafening all with bells,
having issued orders, he quickly entered the assembly hall crowded with officials // KNarm_1.45 //
<s>Marīci</s> (Mirage), having occupied a prominent position through the people's misfortunes,
saw from afar an official messenger approaching on business // KNarm_1.46 //
With inauspicious footwear, bearing a circular instrument for evicting temples,
wearing a raised cap decorated with an arrangement of extremely fine petals, // KNarm_1.47 //
of the hue of flax-flowers, with a body-garment soft to the touch,
wrapped in a thick cotton cloth fragrant with genuine musk, // KNarm_1.48 //
with a golden triple-twisted bracelet placed on his finger,
making grimaces from sighing due to fatigue from the long journey, // KNarm_1.49 //
seeing that slanderous 'devotee' approaching nearby,

children.text: utthāya harṣādālambya pāṇau pārśve nyaveśayat // KNarm_1.50 //
children.translated_text: he rose joyfully, took him by the hand, and seated him at his side // KNarm_1.50 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends the description of] the Household Steward.

children.translated_text: Obeisance to those slanderers, by whose grace the officials,
though stationed far away, become possessed of a thousand ears and eyes // KNarm_1.51 //
He said: 'Having heard that you are at the forefront of the powerful,
I have come from the temple—this one, a guide to the path of revenue // KNarm_1.52 //
'Whatever cloth, ornaments, jewels, and such are in the temples,
all that exists without exception, I shall make known to you // KNarm_1.53 //
'In <s>Vijayeśvara</s>, <s>Vārāha</s>, <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, and other [temples] there exists
a revenue, replete and overflowing, by the accumulation of your good fortune // KNarm_1.54 //
'Fearless in the face of censure, unscrupulous in sins,

children.text: tatra tīkṣṇo bhṛśaṃ śaśvatkriyatāṃ paripālakaḥ // KNarm_1.55 //
children.translated_text: let a most fierce and perpetual guardian be appointed there // KNarm_1.55 //

children.text: sa cāsti bhuvi vikhyātaḥ kāyastho bhavatā samaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'There is also on earth a well-known <s>Kāyastha</s>, your equal—

children.text: vinā dhanaṃ vināyāsaṃ sarvasvaharaṇaṃ vinā // KNarm_1.56 //
children.translated_text: for whom neither wealth, nor effort, nor confiscation of everything is spared // KNarm_1.56 //

children.text: brahmahatyā na gaṇyante govadheṣu kathaiva kā /
children.translated_text: 'Brahmin-slayings are not counted [as sin by him]; what need to speak of cow-slaughter?
He by whom, out of devotion to the master, people are uprooted from their very roots // KNarm_1.57 //

children.text: anye 'pi santi sarvatra tadvidhastu na labhyate /
children.translated_text: 'Others too exist everywhere, but one of his kind is not to be found—

children.text: nītaḥ svajanako yena nidhanaṃ bandhane dhanī // KNarm_1.58 //
children.translated_text: he by whom his own father was brought to death while wealthy, in prison // KNarm_1.58 //

children.text: yadi nāma bhavatpuṇyaiḥ sa sameṣyati madgirā /
children.translated_text: 'If indeed by your merit he comes at my word,
then know your own house to be a treasury of riches at your pleasure' // KNarm_1.59 //
To him speaking thus, having whispered arrangements in his ear repeatedly,
the great one said to him: 'Let him be brought immediately!' // KNarm_1.60 //
Then he, hastily, with two or three respectful comings and goings,
brought that sinful guardian, having ascertained [him] with certainty // KNarm_1.61 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends the description of] the Temple-evictor, or Procurer.

children.translated_text: With neck stiffly raised like wood, with motionless upward-gazing eyes,
wearing a jaundice-green head-cloth and tunic, // KNarm_1.62 //
with a great hanging [belly] resembling the bosom of a privy,
pervaded by a belly like a cave, a house of flesh, // KNarm_1.63 //
of fierce arrogance, great wrath, life-seizing, irresistible,

children.text: sopadravaḥ sopatāpaḥ sannipāta iva jvaraḥ // KNarm_1.64 //
children.translated_text: afflicting and tormenting, like a fever of the <s>sannipāta</s> (combined humors) type, // KNarm_1.64 //

children.text: sa mahāntaṃ samāsādya duḥsahaṃ daṃśanaṃ viṭam /
children.translated_text: he, having approached the great, unbearable, biting villain,
and having subdued him effortlessly, obtained many temples // KNarm_1.65 //
Then, with embodied exertions as his sudden vanguard,

children.text: argha velāṃ yayau kartumasaṅkhyaiḥ parivāritaḥ // KNarm_1.66 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by countless [followers], he went to perform the revenue assessment // KNarm_1.66 //
'This rogue is <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> (Gold-eye, the demon), remembering ancient enmity,

children.text: devānavāptaḥ saṃhartumiti taṃ bubudhe janaḥ // KNarm_1.67 //
children.translated_text: come to destroy the gods!'—thus did the people understand him // KNarm_1.67 //
When the wealthy had fled from the temple out of fear,
the impoverished temple-dwellers again approached him // KNarm_1.68 //
When the soldiers, busy breaking open bolted doors and gates,
had begun the great festival of plundering household goods and such, // KNarm_1.69 //
there arose from the housewives suddenly stripped of their garments,
and from the terrified children, a piteous sound of weeping // KNarm_1.70 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends the description of] the Guardian.

children.translated_text: Then there came one, stumbling in his gait from the great joy long attained,
thin, resembling <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), dusty, his belly wounded by hunger, // KNarm_1.71 //
with a head-cloth full of holes, its ragged edges dangling,
wearing a body-garment sewn with a hundred patches and smeared with grime, // KNarm_1.72 //
his skirt-edge held in place by a belt covered with worn and tattered cloth,
the rogue, pained by dried-up sandals obtained through begging, // KNarm_1.73 //
a writing-officer, though possessing nothing, proud of his writing refinement,
appointed by the Guardian, like a serpent feeding on air, // KNarm_1.74 //
his wife, her waist-region covered with torn cloth fragments,
with lamp-black smeared on her nose-tip, wearing dangling clay ear-ornaments, // KNarm_1.75 //
angry because her children were hungry, her head covered with half a winnowing-fan,

children.text: samutthāya saśūtkāraṃ kaṣantī bahuśaḥ sphijau // KNarm_1.76 //
children.translated_text: rising and scratching her buttocks repeatedly with hissing sounds, // KNarm_1.76 //
when her husband obtained his position after long [waiting], delighted, gathering [things] from here and there,
with scattered cakes, incense, and the like, she worshipped <s>Gaṇādhipa</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) // KNarm_1.77 //
He too, attentively hearing the various messages and instructions of the master,
with hand extended to receive [bribes], wrote documents without hesitation // KNarm_1.78 //
His pen racing, shrieking loudly like a beaten monkey,
counting <s>dīnāras</s> (gold coins) quickly, he issued two hundred documents // KNarm_1.79 //
Whatever serves the needs of the Guardian's feet [i.e., servants]—
ladle, cushion, tablet, pot, vessel, and basket— // KNarm_1.80 //
through the granting of such documents, he attained the highest renown;
and in no time he became well-fed, with palms full [of bribes], arrogant with pride // KNarm_1.81 //
Reading aloud the document-leaves with rolling eyes,
he made various grotesque expressions with diverse contractions of eyebrows and eyes // KNarm_1.82 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends the description of] the Writing-master.

children.translated_text: Then, having obtained the arrangement of breaking the umbrella of the mediator,
the Treasury Scribe came, requested by <s>Bhaṭṭa Bhāgavata</s> // KNarm_1.83 //
He, proud, having abandoned rags through the profits from death-dues,
with half his forehead whitened by the arrangement of his head-cloth, // KNarm_1.84 //
intent on the destruction of the revenue of all temples and villages,
having reduced all ... to mere ropes through the Guardian, // KNarm_1.85 //
having arrived, he issued a long six-month assessment for autumn

children.text: yasyā madhye 'sti likhitaṃ sārdhaṃ lakṣacatuṣṭayam // KNarm_1.86 //
children.translated_text: in the middle of which is written four and a half <s>lakṣas</s> (hundred thousands).
Then, asked about the means for his own profit, with an agreement of acceptance,
he spoke, satisfied with his share, having assumed some semblance of good faith:
"In this temple, those various well-known caretakers,
having sold all their possessions, have departed as my adversaries.
But today, out of affection, a favor must be done by me for you,

children.text: kulācāryaḥ sa bhagavāneko hi gururāvayoḥ // KNarm_1.89 //
children.translated_text: for that revered one is the family preceptor, indeed the sole <s>guru</s> of us both.
Through gifts, by five or six accepted wicked wheel-turners,

children.text: bhujyate nikhilaṃ devadravyaṃ bhuktiśca pārṣadī // KNarm_1.90 //
children.translated_text: all the temple property is enjoyed, and the assembly's revenue too.
Whatever remains unsold in the temple precinct,
all that, with his consent alone, is enjoyed by you as your own.

children.text: tathā hi tāmrajaḥ pūrvaṃ mahān nīto ghaṭo mayā /
children.translated_text: For instance, a large copper pot was previously taken by me,
and out of devotion, from a hundredth part of it, a bell was made for the temple.

children.text: kālena ghaṇṭāṃ vikrīya tadaṃśena kṛtā ghaṭī /
children.translated_text: In time, having sold the bell, from that portion a small pot was made;

children.text: krameṇa bhakṣitā sāpi kṛtā śeṣeṇa ghaṇṭikā // KNarm_1.93 //
children.translated_text: gradually that too was consumed, and from the remainder a small bell was made.
Over time, that too was ground down and made into a tiny tinkling ornament;

children.text: iti kṛtvā tataḥ stokaghaṇṭāṃśaḥ paripālitaḥ // KNarm_1.94 //
children.translated_text: thus, having done so, a small portion of the bell was preserved.
Thus a four-armed robbery is carried out under the guise of <s>Śiva</s>-worship.
There are thousands of grains here; let Your Honor conduct

children.text: krayavikrayikā nāma tato vijñapyase mayā // KNarm_1.95 //
children.translated_text: the so-called buying and selling—therefore I beseech you."
Thus, through those hundreds of various stratagems spoken by him, the caretaker,
like an old rat gnawing a walnut, emptied the temple.

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the tale of] the treasury clerk.

children.translated_text: Now, another one, inclined toward heaps of wealth, skilled in robbing the virtuous,
that expert in administration obtained a village for the suppression of calamities.
In his house, whose belly was like great <s>Raurava</s> (hell), covered with filth,
with a broken, cracked water-pot at its nose-tip as its great treasure,
whose old door, tied with ropes, rattled and clattered,
in that house, like the hollow of a hen—there was his dwelling.
Wearing a turban-wrapping made of pieces of a burnt blanket,
with worn-out, tattered sandals gnawed by dogs at the tips, limping, walking slowly,
carrying rags, sesame, <s>darbha</s> grass, <s>pavitra</s> rings, and <s>arghya</s> vessels,
bearing a wooden tray—full, broken, gnawed by rats,
bathing, with his tuft of hair shaking from his <s>japa</s> (recitation), established in the path of good conduct,
for half the day he recited hymns, having gone to the temple.
Circumambulating cows, bowing to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, observing the <s>Dvādaśī</s> vow,
he gave to the poor on the road, with great effort, a single small coin.
By fate, when an appointment came for that very administrator,
his house became filled with furniture, vessels, and the like.
In winter, his neighbors who would not give him a single coal,
now gave him unsolicited clothing, ornaments, and desired things.
Then his house, whitewashed with plaster, with swept courtyards,
became a mansion with many servants, a temple with vermilion-painted interiors.
His wife, her complexion having acquired new beauty and charm from fine foods,
became in a few days equal to an <s>Apsaras</s> (celestial nymph).
Then too, as he went to the village, baskets, bedding, and such
came forth before him—an umbrella, a water-pot, a copper vessel,
a spear, a fly-whisk, a bell, a copper plate, sandals,
a leather bag, the Lord's foot-sandals, birch-bark bellows, and ladles,
a rosary, an ink-pot, a mirror, a bathing cloth,
boxes, pouches, swords, wooden sandals, a book of <s>mantras</s>,
an astrological chart, a leaf-blade, a red blanket,
a sacred thread cord, a lute string, a needle, a pen-knife,
sweet flag, a resin amulet, a razor, a <s>yoga</s> mat,
hymns and <s>mantras</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s> clay, a <s>bilva</s>-wood plate of offerings—
all this equipment and paraphernalia, gathered together before him, went forth,
brought from here and there by one with no intention of returning it.
With hands raised high holding a vine-whip, on a hired horse,
with the jingling strike of his heels, making his face bold repeatedly,
as if threatening the people, as if making a display,
with loose, thick garments, he went to the town in exultation.
Then he entered the village, in washed white rags,

children.text: kṣayāya grāmyamatsyānāṃ vṛddho baka ivāgataḥ // KNarm_1.116 //
children.translated_text: like an old crane come for the destruction of the village fish.
Then, under the pretext of food offerings and such practices, by the thousands,
treasures came before him, as if before <s>Kubera</s> (lord of wealth) himself.
A <s>yogī</s> in thoughts of seizing, a practitioner in birch-bark schemes,
separated from his own wife, an enjoyer of the riches of hell.
Not useful in producing results, merely zealous in faults,

children.text: aśo[kaḥ] satataṃ rogī niyogī jayati prabhuḥ // KNarm_1.119 //
children.translated_text: always sickly yet without sorrow—thus the appointed master prevails!
Among thousands of tree-climbers and generally hundreds of exhausted ones,
in the village, for those ruined by him, it became like hell.
He who made confinement unto death as punishment for cattle offenses—

children.text: kā nāma gaṇanā tasya nṛṣu sarvāparādhiṣu // KNarm_1.121 //
children.translated_text: what count was there for him among men, all being offenders?
Confiscation of all property, imprisonment, punishment, demolition of houses—

children.text: iti tasya mukhādghoraṃ na cacāla vacaḥ sadā // KNarm_1.122 //
children.translated_text: such terrible words never departed from his mouth.

children.text: pañcaṣāḥ satataṃ tasya karabhā iva bhārikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Five or six porters, constantly like camels carrying loads for him—
ghee, honey, gold coins, pepper, fresh ginger, rock salt,
mung beans, blankets, peacock feathers, sandals, rams, birds,
lotus stalks, grapes, jars of honey, walnuts, couches, and seats,
bronze, copper, iron, and various household utensils—
those tireless ones carried to his house whatever his word demanded.
Letters of remission and penalty that arrived from the master,

children.text: sādhikṣepaṃ sathūtkāraṃ cakāra tilaśo nakhaiḥ // KNarm_1.126 //
children.translated_text: he, with contempt and haughtiness, tore to tiny pieces with his nails.
Always eating meat and ghee, when a royal officer was present,
he hypocritically ate alone two handfuls of unsalted mung beans.

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the tale of] the highway superintendent or the trader.

children.translated_text: Dismissing the chief clerk, who was incurable in his thefts,

children.text: cakāra vārikaṃ so 'tha cikitsācaturaṃ param // KNarm_1.128 //
children.translated_text: he then appointed as water-superintendent another, clever in remedies.
That one, freed by him from twelve years of imprisonment,
being expert in visible letters, wrote forgeries and frauds.

children.text: kṛttāṅguṣṭhaḥ sa vāmena pāṇinā diviro rahaḥ /
children.translated_text: With his thumb cut off, that clerk, with his left hand, secretly

children.text: khala..sya gṛhaṃ gatvā vidadhe bhūrjayojanam // KNarm_1.130 //
children.translated_text: going to the house of the rogue, prepared a birch-bark scheme.
Taking a pot of liquor between his two knees,
sipping measured amounts repeatedly, slowly drinking more and more,
he wrote with the line of his pen, making loud chirping sounds,
with the tip of his last finger, noisily, with flourished letters.
Plundering the regular and occasional expenses for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, cows, and gods,
reciting what was spoken by the glorious <s>Guru</s> Cobbler and Lord of the Sick—
singing repeatedly in a hoarse voice, crying out with an excess of devotion to <s>Śiva</s>,
crushing lice with the tip of his nail, repeatedly picking them from his blanket,
sighing again and again, condemning the ways of the world,
he, filled with joy, balanced the expenditure with the income.
Possessed like a <s>vetāla</s> (vampire spirit), he trembled, intoxicated with liquor,
adorned with a garland of bangles mixed with disheveled cloth strips.
Agitated by the cracking sounds of thick birch-bark and loud music,
with his two testicles protruding through holes in his loincloth,
his body splattered with streaks from a rolling full ink-pot,

children.text: nanarta diviraḥ kṣībo nagno bhagnabṛsīghaṭaḥ // KNarm_1.138 //
children.translated_text: the clerk danced drunk, naked, with broken cushion and pot.
Dusty, with limbs smeared with filth, he rose up like a <s>piśāca</s> (demon),
and rejoiced, filled with intoxication, at having stolen people's livelihoods.
With the clinking and clattering sounds of armpit-scratching and slapping,
some shoulder-drum revelry of his continued in solitude for a long time.

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the tale of] the village clerk.

children.translated_text: Constantly occupied with that thieving clerk,
the forest of people blazed, like fire together with wind.
Before long, when that one's house became filled with great wealth,
his wife, adorned, garlanded, devoted to the ritual of betel-leaf,
the housewife, absorbed in the mirror, gazing at the royal road,
bore, in his absence, the pride of a king's consort.

children.text: hāro bhārāyate hematāṭaṅkaṃ me na vallabham /
children.translated_text: "The necklace is burdensome to me; the gold ear-ornament is not to my liking;
fie upon the heavy gold chain fit for a merchant's wife!"
"Only a single pearl necklace is lovely—this elegant one is my favorite"—

children.text: iti darpagirā tasyā nābhavat kasya vismayaḥ // KNarm_1.145 //
children.translated_text: at such proud words of hers, who was not amazed?
"Ah, the blessed ink is the giver of success in all endeavors!
Ah, how powerful is some pen, the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (goddess of wealth)!"
"She who drank begged-for gruel from a broken, sewn stone vessel—
that very one now drinks musk-scented honey from a silver cup!"
Thus, looking down from the upper story at the <s>Kāyastha</s> (scribe-caste) beauty,
the well-born women, daughters of the neighbors, sang.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>parihāsa</s> (jest) of the <s>Narmamālā</s>.
The Second Jest.

children.translated_text: She too, with eyes like a young doe, with overpowering youth,

children.text: bhidyamāneva darpeṇa na dadarśa vasundharām // KNarm_2.1 //
children.translated_text: as if bursting with pride, did not see the earth.
Hostile to her mother-in-law's household, a young neighbor-woman,
fond of jest and gossip, attached to song and music,
her limbs anointed with lovely fragrance, she did not wear a bodice,
displaying the fullness of her breasts, with her head-cloth half-slipped.
Yawning, turning aside, with sidelong glances,
the flirtatious woman with rolling eyes looked at the people, her triple fold of skin rippling.
Seeing her, easy to win, with playful eyes,
the libertines wandered near her house, going back and forth without purpose.
For a long time, those desirous of her, adorned in colorful garments,
spending on fragrant oils, betel, incense, and such,
with hopes fixed on the official's wealth, eager to obtain the jewel of a woman,
making hundreds of gestures—smiles, narrowing of eyes, and such,
with steps unknown even to experts, watching for an opening—
those serpents, wishing to bite, moved with playful, sinuous gaits.
Going to an empty shrine, well-known adulterers,
two or three of them, pondered the means of union with the neighbor's wife.
One libertine said there: "She is easily obtainable, no doubt—

children.text: khalvāṭaṃ tundilaṃ vṛddhaṃ svapatiṃ sahate katham // KNarm_2.10 //
children.translated_text: how can she endure her husband, who is bald, pot-bellied, and old?
Always traveling, greedy, jealous, incapable in love,
smelling of a drunken goat, frequently spitting, a rogue—
she is not barren from suppression of children, nor has her youth faded,

children.text: na ca duḥkhābhibhūtāsau rāgadagdhā na lakṣyate // KNarm_2.12 //
children.translated_text: nor is she afflicted by suffering—is she not seen to be burning with passion?
Even with these faults in him, ill-natured women do not come [easily]."
Another said: "You have thought with purpose,

children.text: pratyāsattyā paricaye kintu yatno vidhīyatām // KNarm_2.13 //
children.translated_text: but let effort be made to establish familiarity through proximity.
Without weddings, sacrifices, pilgrimages, temple festivals, and processions,
familiarity cannot be obtained in approaching another's wife.
Long gazing, repeatedly tossing playful curls,
conversations connected with her under hidden pretexts, revealing one's generosity,
establishing one's reputation for enjoyment, good fortune, and fame,
speaking softly and slowly, showing respect for her words,
fixing one's gaze on her face, kissing and embracing her child,
providing her crafts, looking at her clothes and ornaments,
when familiarity is established, offering garlands, betel, and such,

children.text: bhittau nipīḍanaṃ gāḍhaṃ vijane paricumbanam // KNarm_2.18 //
children.translated_text: pressing firmly against the wall, kissing in private,
touching secret parts, and then love-making—these are the means for destroying chastity.

children.text: itthaṃ kā nāma na mayā kṛtā śīlaparāṅmukhī // KNarm_2.19 //
children.translated_text: In this way, whom have I not turned away from virtue?

body.translated_text: An official's wife is always obtainable, always inclined to go with others."
Thus ends [the tale of] the adulterer.

children.translated_text: Then a third one also said: "Everything is indeed in our power,
but in this matter, due to fate's opposition, an obstacle is perceived.
This one, who on the sharp surface of a tablet acts like <s>Citragupta</s>,
causing terror to all livelihoods, a destroyer of the helpless,
with the devices of loads, treasury-chains, torments, and partial ledger-entries—"
By whom the uncouth ones were made to attain the status of cowherds and animal-keepers // <s>KNarm</s> 2.22 //

children.text: na kālo yadi nāmāsau tat kiṃ jīvanahṛnnṛṇām /
children.translated_text: If he is not <s>Kāla</s> (Time/Death) by name, then why does he steal the lives of men?
If he cuts wings... then why is he the destroyer of a single woman? // <s>KNarm</s> 2.23 //
Asking again and again, 'How many have died today? Where?'
That one who lives off the dead, equal to a dog, observes the vow of a <s>Kāpālika</s> // <s>KNarm</s> 2.24 //
His hand is ever raised for seizing, even in dealings with good people,
By us sinful ones, an offering of sesame seeds is given to hell // <s>KNarm</s> 2.25 //
Although he desires his daughter-in-law and is the ornament of the liquor-dealer's family,
Nevertheless, everyone is omniscient when it comes to seeing the faults of others // <s>KNarm</s> 2.26 //
Or rather, I do indeed have a friend who is powerful and dear to the king;

children.text: vāṅmātreṇaiva naḥ sarvaṃ saṃrakṣiṣyati jīvanam // KNarm_2.27 //
children.translated_text: By mere words alone, he will protect all our lives // <s>KNarm</s> 2.27 //
Arsonists, slayers of cows, women, children, and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> —
Many such servants of mere rumors from distant lands were protected by him // <s>KNarm</s> 2.28 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the description of] the livelihood-secretary.

children.translated_text: He enters the house of the official's wife with great boldness;

children.text: eṣā śramaṇikā nityaṃ kuṭṭanī vajrayoginī // KNarm_2.29 //
children.translated_text: 'This female ascetic is always a procuress, a <s>Vajrayoginī</s>' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.29 //
She who is the mother of love-spells, the accomplished messenger of paramours,
The covenant-deity of women in initiations into acquiring men // <s>KNarm</s> 2.30 //
She would quickly deceive even <s>Arundhatī</s> with ease;

children.text: purāṇapuṃścalī sā hi jāhnavīṃ manyate tṛṇam // KNarm_2.31 //
children.translated_text: For she, the ancient harlot, considers the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges) as a mere blade of grass // <s>KNarm</s> 2.31 //
She will fulfill our desire before long —
Having said this, those rogues went to the house of the old female ascetic // <s>KNarm</s> 2.32 //
The female ascetic (<s>Śramaṇikā</s>):
Then one day, in the upper chamber, [seeing] that doe-eyed woman,
His body filled out from eating at charitable feasts, his youth having returned // <s>KNarm</s> 2.33 //
Wearing a large <s>tilaka</s> of burnt sandalwood paste, bearing broad matted locks,
Proud with the slow, arrogant gait [caused by his] peacock-feather sandals // <s>KNarm</s> 2.34 //
With his cloth tucked under his arm, not even touching <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: re re dāsīsutetyādi janaṃ kopena bhartsayan // KNarm_2.35 //
children.translated_text: Angrily rebuking people with cries of 'Hey, you son of a slave-woman!' and such // <s>KNarm</s> 2.35 //
The foolish monastery-preceptor, carrying his almanac, beheld [her],
Suddenly seized with wonder, bitten by <s>Makaraketu</s> (the god of love) // <s>KNarm</s> 2.36 //
Having approached the teacher of the children in the official's household,
He came as a daily letter-teacher for a monthly wage // <s>KNarm</s> 2.37 //
Having gained entry, that rogue, meditating upon her alone, taught —
Though knowing all scripts, he slowly wrote only the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> // <s>KNarm</s> 2.38 //
Out of curiosity, surrounded by the women of the household, he stood facing them,
While the teacher was mentally counting his <s>dīnāras</s> (gold coins) // <s>KNarm</s> 2.39 //
Proud as if omniscient with his recitation of the Hymn to the Eight Avatars,
Saying 'I shall teach the preceptor!' he became even more arrogant // <s>KNarm</s> 2.40 //
May the feet of the Lord protect us — those feet compassionate to the lowest of people,
Destroyers of the other world, bringers of safety in travel // <s>KNarm</s> 2.41 //

children.text: bhābhūto kuṅkumārdrau ^ ^ ^ ^ ^ _ rainaisaddṛśau _ _ _ _ ^ _ _ ^ ^ ^ musimusi lakṣaṇau phenaparvau /
children.translated_text: Radiant, moist with saffron, ... similar to ..., bearing the mark of ..., with foam-joints —

children.text: _ _ _ _ ^ _ _ maṇikanakadharau divyagandhānuliptau saṅgrāmeṇa praviṣṭau palupa ^ ^ ^ nau labhyatāṃ rājyalakṣmīḥ // KNarm_2.42 //
children.translated_text: ... bearing jewels and gold, anointed with divine fragrance, having entered in battle ... may the royal fortune be obtained! // <s>KNarm</s> 2.42 //
Of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>, a bilva-fruit and a bull, of the full pitchers,
Five sandal-pastes ... a cloth-binding shall be [prepared] // <s>KNarm</s> 2.43 //

children.text: ityādi dattvā bālānāṃ nityaṃ phalahakeṣu saḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus given such things daily to children for trifling rewards,
He stays for a year without worry, counting his monthly salary // <s>KNarm</s> 2.44 //
Cutting, writing, applying needle-bandage and ointment —

children.text: kurvanna *vetti purataḥ sthitānno vā kumārakān // KNarm_2.45 //
children.translated_text: Doing all this, he does not notice whether children are standing before him or not // <s>KNarm</s> 2.45 //
When addressed as 'Teacher,' he speaks, burning with the fire of anger:
'Am I a musician or a leather-worker to you?' — thus he speaks harshly // <s>KNarm</s> 2.46 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the description of] the boys' teacher.

children.translated_text: Smiling, with smiling conversation, frequently arranging social gatherings —

children.text: niyogikāntā paśyantī daiśikaṃ nācalat tataḥ // KNarm_2.47 //
children.translated_text: The official's wife, seeing the preceptor, did not move from her spot // <s>KNarm</s> 2.47 //
Though he understood the language spoken by the various women,

children.text: kiṃ bhaṇantīti papraccha prollasadbhrūlato muhuḥ // KNarm_2.48 //
children.translated_text: He asked again and again, 'What are they saying?' with his eyebrows raised playfully // <s>KNarm</s> 2.48 //
He, by their jesting, laughter, gentle reproaches, and mockeries,
Being teased by those intoxicated women, became one with a laughing face // <s>KNarm</s> 2.49 //

children.text: nāyaṃ kiñcinmahābhāgo jānāti na ca budhyate /
children.translated_text: 'This greatly fortunate one neither knows anything nor understands' —

children.text: iti no bhejire lajjā vivastrā api tasya tāḥ // KNarm_2.50 //
children.translated_text: Thinking thus, they felt no shame, even unclothed, before him // <s>KNarm</s> 2.50 //
He, observing the vow of <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, then ...

children.text: tāsāṃ goṣṭhīrasābhijñaḥ stanau pasparśa pāṇinā // KNarm_2.51 //
children.translated_text: Knowing the pleasure of their gatherings, he touched their breasts with his hand // <s>KNarm</s> 2.51 //
That young man, like a stud-horse released among mares,

children.text: siṣeve lalanāḥ sarvāḥ proṣitasya niyoginaḥ // KNarm_2.52 //
children.translated_text: Enjoyed all the women of the absent official // <s>KNarm</s> 2.52 //

children.text: bhrātṛjāyāṃ svasāraṃ ca tāṃ ca bhāryāṃ mṛgīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: The brother's wife, the sister, and that doe-eyed wife,
And others too — the preceptor freely desired all of them always // <s>KNarm</s> 2.53 //
Those noble women, initiated by that teacher of paramours,
Became promiscuous, established in the vow of non-discrimination // <s>KNarm</s> 2.54 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the description of] the monastery-preceptor.

children.translated_text: Through that female ascetic's mediation, those rogues too, having made their effort,

children.text: dhūrtāḥ svādhīnatāṃ prāptāṃ svairiṇīṃ tāṃ siṣevire // KNarm_2.55 //
children.translated_text: The scoundrels enjoyed that wanton woman who had become independent // <s>KNarm</s> 2.55 //
Then the official, longing, remembering that beloved young woman,
Entered quickly in paid garments, under the pretext of village-healing // <s>KNarm</s> 2.56 //
He, having brought ghee, honey, and clarified butter for service,
Filled the town with burden-carriers and wealthy men out of fear // <s>KNarm</s> 2.57 //
Seeing him arrived after a long time, she who had known many lovers —
[Seeing him] fat, rustic, near illness, like a vessel full to the brim with water // <s>KNarm</s> 2.58 //
And that wealth of goat's ghee, curds, cheese, and honey —
That wife wept with one eye and laughed with the other // <s>KNarm</s> 2.59 //
'This beautiful cloth has been bought, and ornaments for you' —

children.text: tasyetivādino dṛptā sā cakre sarvamaśrutam // KNarm_2.60 //
children.translated_text: As he said this, she proudly made all his words as if unheard // <s>KNarm</s> 2.60 //
She, with a bandage tied under the pretext of a headache,
Groaning loudly, would not stay by her husband's side // <s>KNarm</s> 2.61 //
Then, in the house filled with the clamor of garlands of chattering gossips,
In his house, there was a great festival with busy village-servants // <s>KNarm</s> 2.62 //
At day's end, eating much food, badly intoxicated by red wine,

children.text: niyogī śayane tasthau kumbhakarṇa ivāparaḥ // KNarm_2.63 //
children.translated_text: The official lay in bed like another <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s> // <s>KNarm</s> 2.63 //
Then, coming with difficulty as if at the end of the night, his wife,
Was anxious at embrace, her face turned away at kisses // <s>KNarm</s> 2.64 //
Blocking the touch of her loins, motionless with crossed thighs,

children.text: gṛhavyāpārakhinneva nidrāṃ cakre mudhaiva sā // KNarm_2.65 //
children.translated_text: As if tired from household chores, she simply fell asleep // <s>KNarm</s> 2.65 //
Then, when dawn spread, with birch-bark vessels and such placed before her,
Complaining of pain in all her limbs, she also feigned exhaustion // <s>KNarm</s> 2.66 //
Then a physician was summoned by the servants — one fond of wine and meat,
Thinking that by fate a treasure had come into his hands, he arrived // <s>KNarm</s> 2.67 //

body.translated_text: The woman with her husband (<s>Sabhārtṛkā</s>):

children.translated_text: Homage to the physician who is devoid of learning and who causes harm,
Who has killed many people, like a serpent bringing untimely death // <s>KNarm</s> 2.68 //
Wandering through a hundred houses quickly, panting as if burdened,
Repeatedly wiping the sweat from his forehead with his hand // <s>KNarm</s> 2.69 //
Carrying a rag with names of medicinal formulas written on it,
He who has come as if a deputy from the presence of the superintendent of <s>Kṛtānta</s> (Death) // <s>KNarm</s> 2.70 //
A healer of wealth and lives, but unable to heal diseases,

children.text: ājīvamīśvaraḥ śūlī yena na tyajyate janaḥ // KNarm_2.71 //
children.translated_text: A lord of livelihood, a tormentor, by whom people are never abandoned // <s>KNarm</s> 2.71 //

children.text: sa vaidyaḥ kālakūṭo vā vyālo vetāla eva vā /
children.translated_text: Is that physician <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison), a serpent, or a <s>Vetāla</s> (demon)?

children.text: bhūyasā yāti māṃsena yaḥ kṣipramanukūlatām // KNarm_2.72 //
children.translated_text: He who quickly becomes favorable only with an abundance of meat // <s>KNarm</s> 2.72 //
That physician himself is an angry wind that causes the destruction of life,
One who washes away the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors) by touch of hand, himself with weakened senses // <s>KNarm</s> 2.73 //
What can be said of the 'teacher of life' for men whom he forces into difficult austerities and renunciation?

children.text: sthitaṃ bhuktaṃ nu pītaṃ nu vaidyeneti pralāpinaḥ // KNarm_2.74 //
children.translated_text: 'Has he stood? Has he eaten? Has he drunk?' — thus prattles the physician // <s>KNarm</s> 2.74 //
Which [illnesses] the physician, who lives off others' misfortunes, arranges with effort —
In city festivals, processions, and weddings, from excessive eating,

children.text: janatā yāti yanmāndyaṃ tadvaidyasya śaneḥ phalam // KNarm_2.75 //
children.translated_text: The lethargy that people experience — that is the fruit of <s>Śani</s> (Saturn) for the physician // <s>KNarm</s> 2.75 //
Touching the private parts of women, eating excessively, destroying lives —

children.text: nṛṇāṃ tridoṣakṛtsatyaṃ vaidya eva na tu jvaraḥ // KNarm_2.76 //
children.translated_text: Truly, it is the physician who creates the three <s>doṣas</s> (humors) in people, not the fever // <s>KNarm</s> 2.76 //
Physicians devoid of learning, powerful <s>Kāyasthas</s> (scribes),
And teachers of bad conduct — these are the causes of the people's destruction // <s>KNarm</s> 2.77 //

children.text: upasṛtya sa pasparśa stanau tasyāḥ susaṃhatau /
children.translated_text: Approaching, he touched her two well-formed breasts,
Hard and constantly touched — the villain touched them as if inspecting something even harder // <s>KNarm</s> 2.78 //

children.text: laṅghanaṃ sahate naiṣā hitaṃ śūle na vṛṃhaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'She cannot bear fasting; in her pain, nourishment is not beneficial;

children.text: karotu mama cintāsu sarvāhāraṃ mayā saha // KNarm_2.79 //
children.translated_text: Let her take all food with me, under my care' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.79 //

children.text: jaḍā hyasyāḥ sthitā buddhirdhātuśca viṣamaḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For her mind is dull, and her humoral balance is disturbed;

children.text: tasmātsnigdhā dadhi pūrvamatra yojyaṃ saśarkaram // KNarm_2.80 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, first a gentle regimen of yogurt mixed with sugar should be prescribed here' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.80 //
When the lord of physicians had thus spoken, the women quickly and excitedly
Summoned with prostrations the astrologer, who arrived // <s>KNarm</s> 2.81 //

body.translated_text: The physician (<s>Vaidya</s>):

children.translated_text: Homage to that one versed in the science of astrology, who has the eye of knowledge —

children.text: varṣaṃ pṛcchatyavarṣaṃ vā dhīvarānyo vinaṣṭadhīḥ // KNarm_2.82 //
children.translated_text: Another fool of destroyed intellect who asks whether it will rain or not // <s>KNarm</s> 2.82 //
Having made no effort even in counting the planets, constellations, and stars,
Carrying an almanac for the pretense of knowing past and future // <s>KNarm</s> 2.83 //
'Within a span of three years, there will be some expenditure of wealth for you,
And fever and eye-trouble, and also unexpected gains' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.84 //

children.text: na kaścidupakāraṃ te manyate śatravaśca te /
children.translated_text: 'No one appreciates your kindness, and you have enemies;

children.text: santi tebhyo bhayaṃ deharakṣāyāṃ naiva bādhate // KNarm_2.85 //
children.translated_text: There is danger from them, but it does not at all harm your physical safety' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.85 //

children.text: durbalo dṛśyase bhrātaryūṣaṃ na kuruṣe katham /
children.translated_text: 'You look weak, brother — why don't you make broth?

children.text: apyasti kāmalā nūnaṃ tāṃ mantreṇa nudāmyaham // KNarm_2.86 //
children.translated_text: Perhaps you surely have jaundice — I shall drive it away with a <s>mantra</s>' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.86 //
Thus, mixing common knowledge with <s>mantra</s>-healing and medicine,
He who, disregarding the science of astrology, robs the simple-minded // <s>KNarm</s> 2.87 //
Though knowing the previous conduct of the official's wife from public rumor,

children.text: dhūrto dhūlipaṭe cakre rāśicakraṃ mudhaiva saḥ // KNarm_2.88 //
children.translated_text: That rogue drew a zodiacal chart on a dust-cloth entirely in vain // <s>KNarm</s> 2.88 //
When the official threw there a heap of gold coins like flowers,
Stiff with pretense, he stood for a long time, absorbed in counting on his fingers // <s>KNarm</s> 2.89 //
Then he spoke very slowly, repeatedly raising his eyebrows:
'This pale-faced woman is afflicted by the demon of desire' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.90 //
'The demon that causes amorous passion in women is irresistible;
Again, bathing naked in an empty house, by a <s>Guhyaka</s> (spirit),
She has been seized — this I see in the chart, due to the conjunction of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus)' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.91 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends [the description of] the astrologer (<s>Gaṇaka</s>).

children.translated_text: Then, when the astrologer had departed and the worship of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) was being contemplated,
With straw sticking out of his clothes, gray with dust from foot to head // <s>KNarm</s> 2.92 //
With his waist bound by a rope, rustic, with worn-out ornaments...,

children.text: visṛṣṭaṃ tatsahāyena dadau lekhaṃ niyoginaḥ // KNarm_2.93 //
children.translated_text: His companion delivered the letter sent by the official // <s>KNarm</s> 2.93 //
'Under the pretext of requisition, ten cows were seized by force;

children.text: tāsāṃ madhyān mṛtāḥ pañca pañca śeṣāḥ sthitāḥ khale // KNarm_2.94 //
children.translated_text: Among them, five have died, and five remain at the threshing floor' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.94 //
'For their release, messengers came in haste, enduring even three days;

children.text: tadabhāve 'pi lābhaste grāme daṇḍaḥ patiṣyati // KNarm_2.95 //
children.translated_text: Even in the absence of that, there is gain for you — a fine will fall upon the village' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.95 //
'And he who was held in prison on account of the ghee-channel,
That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too, without food, severe, has met his death' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.96 //
'The writ of property was sent to your feet,

children.text: baddhaṃ mayā tatkalatraṃ mudritaṃ sakalaṃ gṛham // KNarm_2.97 //
children.translated_text: His wife was arrested by me, and the entire house was sealed' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.97 //
'Those deputies whom the superintendent sent on account of the burden-tax,

children.text: pradadau māsavṛttyaiva te mayā tadgṛhe dhṛtāḥ // KNarm_2.98 //
children.translated_text: Those whom he assigned on a monthly stipend — I have detained them in that house' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.98 //
'There is a great heap of grain — come here quickly;
This is the gist — your feet are humbly informed, on Sunday in the month of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.99 //

body.translated_text: The lord of provisions, the quiver-keeper:

children.translated_text: Having that letter read aloud, and hearing of his assistant's diligence,
The official, overflowing with joy, praised his companion // <s>KNarm</s> 2.100 //
He was formerly a Buddhist, then became a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> for the sake of pretense,
And then, for the protection of his wife, he developed devotion to the <s>Kaula</s> <s>Āgama</s> // <s>KNarm</s> 2.101 //
He brought a <s>guru</s> who was the abode of pride, pretense, and greed,
A <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) of initiation and vows for deception, trickery, and wantonness // <s>KNarm</s> 2.102 //
Salutations to the lord-<s>guru</s> who steals wealth and wives,
To the agitator, the all-devouring one, like a <s>Yakṣa</s>, the lord of the night // <s>KNarm</s> 2.103 //
With half a <s>sindūra</s>-leaf and a bunch of flowers placed on his forehead,
With his great forehead-skull always moist with dots and sub-dots of paste // <s>KNarm</s> 2.104 //
With only a small topknot tied at the root of his ear,
with saffron-marked ear-tips, glass eyes, and a massive jaw, // <s>KNarm</s> 2.105 //
Bald, with sparse beard, long-tongued, sometimes stumbling,
bearing a face resembling the vulva of an old buffalo, // <s>KNarm</s> 2.106 //
He who in an instant drinks a pot of wine with gurgling sounds—
with what can the thickness of his throat-channel be compared? // <s>KNarm</s> 2.107 //
Wearing a <s>yogapaṭṭaka</s> (yogic cloth) soiled with the foul smell of wine and meat,
his chest full like breasts, having the form of a <s>Rākṣasa</s>, // <s>KNarm</s> 2.108 //
Adorned with a deep navel-cavity filled with <s>sindūra</s>,
his great belly stuffed with <s>lopikā</s> cakes, fish, and milk-porridge, // <s>KNarm</s> 2.109 //
Releasing unbearable belches freshly odorous from indigestion caused by honey and meat,
emitting smoky burps and rumblings like an agitated cloud, // <s>KNarm</s> 2.110 //
A <s>guru</s> heavy with the heaviest ignorance, blameworthy, his intellect blinded by wine,
like <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (Ego) itself arrived in bodily form, he appeared, // <s>KNarm</s> 2.111 //
Heavy in form, heavy in speech, heavy with sloth and stupidity, exceedingly heavy in the phallus, heavy in the cave of his mouth, beard, belly, and buttocks,

children.text: veśyākāminiyogivañcanaguruḥ sadvṛttaśūnyo guruś citraṃ sarvaguruḥ śivoditamahāśikṣāsu nityaṃ laghuḥ // KNarm_2.112 //
children.translated_text: a <s>guru</s> heavy in deceiving courtesans, lovers, and yogis; a <s>guru</s> devoid of good conduct—wonderful!—heavy in everything, yet always light in the great teachings of <s>Śiva</s>! // <s>KNarm</s> 2.112 //

children.text: api nāma sa jāyeta pavitracaritaḥ kṣitau /
children.translated_text: May there be born on earth one of pure conduct,
who has not served such <s>gurus</s>, those repositories of impurity! // <s>KNarm</s> 2.113 //
All fell at his feet, competing to be first,
creating with their heads a commotion like pots rolling in an earthquake. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.114 //
For the protection of his wife and for the increase of his wealth,
the official (<s>niyogin</s>) requested the venerable <s>guru</s> for a sacrificial rite. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.115 //
Having quickly written a short list of offerings with saffron,
pleased, saying 'I shall come in the morning,' he departed with his attendants. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.116 //

body.translated_text: The <s>guru</s>.

children.translated_text: The father-in-law, earnestly invited by the official for the sacrificial supplies—
that sinful court secretary (<s>divira</s>), the revenue officer, then arrived. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.117 //
Salutations to that excellent city-teacher, the serpentine one,

children.text: yasya haste sthitā bhūmiḥ saśailavanakānanā // KNarm_2.118 //
children.translated_text: in whose hand rests the earth with its mountains, forests, and groves! // <s>KNarm</s> 2.118 //

children.text: karoti praśrayaṃ vakti madhuraṃ diviraḥ puraḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>divira</s> shows humility and speaks sweetly in his presence,

children.text: jaracchagalaśṛṅgābhāṃ na ca tyajati vakratām // KNarm_2.119 //
children.translated_text: yet does not abandon his crookedness, like the horns of an old goat. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.119 //
By this court secretary with a pen behind his ear, birch-bark document in hand—
by this <s>āsthāna-divira</s> (court secretary), this blessed earth has been devoured! // <s>KNarm</s> 2.120 //
In vain did the great <s>Varāha</s> display his prowess against the demons,
if this earth, devoured by court secretaries, was not rescued! // <s>KNarm</s> 2.121 //
Rising from the courtesan's bed at dawn, dizzy with wine,

children.text: dhanārthī diviraḥ śastamukhaṃ draṣṭuṃ pratīkṣate // KNarm_2.122 //
children.translated_text: the <s>divira</s>, eager for money, waits to see an auspicious face. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.122 //

children.text: nūnaṃ niśi bhagāpānaṃ karoti diviraḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: Surely the secretary always drinks from the vulva at night,

children.text: prātaḥ prātarmṛdā vaktraṃ kṣālayatyanyathā katham // KNarm_2.123 //
children.translated_text: for why else does he wash his face with clay every morning? // <s>KNarm</s> 2.123 //
Having bathed, holding clay, <s>darbha</s> grass, and sesame, he performs his prayers at length—
the <s>divira</s>, all the while contemplating forged contract documents. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.124 //

children.text: vipraṃ puraḥ samāyāntaṃ thūtkṛtya tvaritaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Spitting upon a Brahmin approaching from the front, the hasty one

children.text: praviśya gehaṃ niryāti śaṅkamānaḥ parābhavam // KNarm_2.125 //
children.translated_text: re-enters his house and comes out again, fearing ill omen. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.125 //
Desiring prosperity, he bows to dog-dung on the road, mistaking it for cow-dung;
and seeking magical powers, he bows to a <s>Caṇḍālī</s> woman with a basket encountered before him. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.126 //
Surrounded by companions who arrived very early, along with troublesome flatterers,
he goes to court calculating roasted meat and beverages. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.127 //
With birch-bark strips dampening the ink that fills his well-stocked vessel,
as if announcing by its smell his future residence in hell, // <s>KNarm</s> 2.128 //
striking honest men with his pen-fang dripping with ink-venom,
the <s>divira</s> plays the sea-monster (<s>makara</s>) in the ocean of the court. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.129 //
Those ink-drops seen falling from his pen
are like collyrium-stained tear-drops of the earth being plundered. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.130 //
Falling headlong from their celestial chariots in heaven, weeping,

children.text: kurvanti pitarastasya yo bhuṅkte divirodanam // KNarm_2.131 //
children.translated_text: are his ancestors—for he devours the funeral offerings. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.131 //

children.text: jāmātuḥ śrīmato dṛṣṭvā sa gṛhaṃ harṣanirbharaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing the house of his prosperous son-in-law, filled with joy,
he thought, 'Perhaps by fate a <s>ṣaṭī</s> (lawsuit) may come about someday!' // <s>KNarm</s> 2.132 //

body.translated_text: The <s>āsthāna-divira</s> (court secretary).

children.translated_text: In his company also appeared the terrifying <s>bhūrja-bhaṭṭas</s> (birch-bark officers),
calculating within his house the ruin of his property. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.133 //
Those who always destroy people along with all things movable and immovable—

children.text: tebhyaḥ pralayakāribhyo bhaṭṭebhyo 'stu namo namaḥ // KNarm_2.134 //
children.translated_text: salutations again and again to those <s>Bhaṭṭas</s>, bringers of cosmic destruction! // <s>KNarm</s> 2.134 //
Dragged by the noose of the <s>ṣaṭī</s> (summons), arriving at court in fear,
an honest man is swallowed by the <s>Bhaṭṭas</s> like bait by fish in water. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.135 //
A person caught in the <s>ṣaṭī</s> by the <s>Bhaṭṭas</s> and their secretary allies
is not released even as a skeleton—like prey caught by blood-drunk dogs. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.136 //
Those <s>Brahma-rākṣasas</s> who were not killed by <s>Rāma</s> on account of their Brahminhood—

children.text: āsthānabhaṭṭāste manye sadā khādanti mānuṣān // KNarm_2.137 //
children.translated_text: they, I think, are the court <s>Bhaṭṭas</s> who always devour humans. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.137 //

children.text: kṛtaḥ parājito jetā jayī yaiśca parājitaḥ /
children.translated_text: They make the defeated into victors and victors into the defeated—

children.text: teṣāṃ svatantravacasāṃ vacasā kena jīvyate // KNarm_2.138 //
children.translated_text: who can survive by the words of those whose words serve only themselves? // <s>KNarm</s> 2.138 //
Those who at the end, surrounded by hell-guardians, have become <s>vetālas</s> (vampires),
with bells placed within their hearts by the <s>ṣaṭī</s>—those <s>Bhaṭṭas</s>, whose messengers of death are they not? // <s>KNarm</s> 2.139 //
Seeing yet blind, speaking yet mute, hearing yet deaf—the wretch,

children.text: utkocena vinā bhaṭṭaściraṃ nidrāyate śaṭhaḥ // KNarm_2.140 //
children.translated_text: without a bribe the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> sleeps for ages, the scoundrel. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.140 //
Consuming bribes, exploiting vulnerabilities, destroying the virtuous,
fueling lawsuits, protecting fraud—such are the marks of a <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.141 //
A leather-worker, brother of a dancing-girl, by association became a dancer;
then, knowing the <s>Gāruḍa-kalpa</s> (snake-charm ritual), he attained the position of crop-guardian. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.142 //
He too obtained the position of palace-guardian of the village chief—
that wretch, a servant of the <s>Kāyastha</s> secretaries of war and peace. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.143 //
Having obtained <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> status as a messenger from his travels to and from <s>Draṅga</s> country,
his sons and grandsons all became court Brahmins. // <s>KNarm</s> 2.144 //
How else would these, like leather-workers, have
a very large bellows in the armpit—a container for <s>ṣaṭī</s>-<s>dīnāras</s> (lawsuit coins)? // <s>KNarm</s> 2.145 //
Thus the court <s>Bhaṭṭas</s> or <s>Sātikas</s>.
Thus ends the second <s>parihāsa</s> (jest) of the <s>Narmamālā</s>.

body.translated_text: The Third <s>Parihāsa</s> (Jest)

children.translated_text: Then at that sacrificial festival, all the relatives of the <s>divira</s>,
along with adorned women, came to the official's house. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.1 //
Chalk, a measuring-rod, a golden vessel, mercury, a gem-casket,
<s>sindūra</s> and other colored powders, five-colored thread, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.2 //
rice flour, a white umbrella, white cloth, a canopy,

children.text: nārācāḥ kṣurikā sūtraṃ darpaṇaṃ vīrakartarī // KNarm_3.3 //
children.translated_text: arrows, a razor, thread, a mirror, and heroic scissors, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.3 //
banners, a fan, a brush, sixteen <s>lakṣas</s> of flowers,
two copper <s>vārdhanī</s> and <s>kalaśa</s> (water-vessels), sesame, oil, and a deer-skin, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.4 //

children.text: sruksruvau samidho darbhā lājāḥ siddhārtakā ghṛtam /
children.translated_text: <s>sruk</s> and <s>sruva</s> (ritual ladles), <s>samidh</s> (kindling sticks), <s>darbha</s> grass, parched rice, mustard seeds, <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee),
<s>bilva</s>, betel-nut, walnut, nutmeg fruits, barley, and <s>akṣata</s> (unbroken rice), // <s>KNarm</s> 3.5 //
incense, saffron, camphor, auspicious herbs, and sandalwood,
sandals, a seat, a couch, bells, a pot, and a fire-pit, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.6 //
wine, meat, liquor, cakes, onions, fish, and rice,
fried pastries, clear broths, sweets, delicacies, and <s>modakas</s> (sweetmeats), // <s>KNarm</s> 3.7 //
plates full of sparrow-meat, milk-pudding, <s>kṛsarā</s> (rice-and-sesame porridge), yogurt,

children.text: daśa kṛṣṇā daśa śvetāśchāgā meṣāścaturdaśa // KNarm_3.8 //
children.translated_text: ten black goats, ten white goats, and fourteen rams, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.8 //
bellows and other such supplies, listed on the document, were in an instant
prepared by the minister-friends and pleasure-companions of the official. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.9 //
Then with constant attention, the disciple made a <s>maṇḍala</s>
decorated with <s>bhaga</s> (vulva) and <s>liṅga</s> symbols, with <s>sindūra</s>-marked intervals. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.10 //
Then the <s>guru</s>, feigning self-contentment, with half-closed rolling eyes,
was held by two disciples by his right and left hands. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.11 //
Followed by about a hundred disciples, he came slowly,
as if the city governor himself had come in person to commit robbery. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.12 //
A leather-worker, a butcher, a potter, a fisherman, a marketplace ascetic,
an old prostitute, a toddy-seller, a liquor-vendor, and an aged debauchee, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.13 //
five citrus-vendors, sick persons, a mint-stamper, and a cook,
a beef-eater, a <s>Bhairavācārya</s>, a <s>Kulācārya</s>, and a weaver, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.14 //
one wearing <s>rudrākṣa</s> beads arranged in a topknot, a <s>Ghaṭila</s> with a cut nose,
a <s>Mahāvratī</s> (great ascetic), a <s>bhagamukha</s> (vulva-faced one), a <s>Śaivācārya</s> with three bells, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.15 //
a naked one, an observer of tidal vows, a silent one, a hymn-composer with knee-bells,
two or three mad women, accompanied by dogs, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.16 //
one smeared with dung, a madman, a spell-caster, an alchemist,
a conjurer, a creeper-medium, a 'wise man,' and a <s>Kāma-tattva</s> practitioner, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.17 //
and other scoundrel-<s>Bhaṭṭas</s> of the <s>guru</s>, servants of drink and food—
they all entered, mouths watering from the aroma of the steaming offerings. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.18 //
Then those destroyers of the raw and the cooked, those all-devouring ones,
the drunken <s>guru-bhaṭṭas</s> caused the depletion of sesame, incense, and ghee. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.19 //

children.text: eko dvau bahavaḥ paścānninyuste bhastrayā tathā /
children.translated_text: First one, then two, then many afterwards carried off with the bellows
the rice flour, barley, walnuts, <s>bilva</s>, <s>arghya</s> offerings, ghee, and sandalwood. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.20 //

body.translated_text: Thus the <s>guru-bhaṭṭas</s>.

children.translated_text: Then his own sister, a widow (<s>raṇḍā</s>), devoted to vows since youth,
was engaged by the official to attend upon the <s>guru</s>'s sacrificial rites. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.21 //
Victorious is the widow with a lotus face, adorned with fresh youth,
who steals the radiance of the full moon's unblemished orb! // <s>KNarm</s> 3.22 //
Bold in passion, with a fierce, upstanding, and delightful love-box,
the widow, broken-hearted without the grinding of fierce love-making— // <s>KNarm</s> 3.23 //
with broad hips like a riverbank, with plump thighs and breasts,
with captivating deer-like eyes, the widow is a feast for the eyes. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.24 //
The widow, with her loosened hair draped over both shoulders, shines
like a lotus-pond covered with bees upon its lotus-blossom faces. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.25 //
Her throat without a necklace-string is charming, her sex is beautiful like gold;
and the widow's ear-loops too are beautiful without ornaments. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.26 //
Without flowers or betel, devoid of ornaments, the widow
seems endowed by <s>Brahmā</s> (the Creator) with an excess of grace alone. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.27 //

children.text: hāreṇa kiṃ sumadhyāyāḥ sukeśyāḥ kusumena kim /
children.translated_text: What need has the slender-waisted one of a necklace? What need has the lovely-haired one of flowers?
What need has the wide-eyed widow of collyrium? What need has the widow of adornment? // <s>KNarm</s> 3.28 //

children.text: kiṃ dharmo yatra no raṇḍā dhiksukhaṃ raṇḍayā vinā /
children.translated_text: What is <s>dharma</s> where there is no widow? Shame on pleasure without a widow!

children.text: raṇḍāhīno 'stu mā mokṣaḥ prauḍhairityuditaṃ viṭaiḥ // KNarm_3.29 //
children.translated_text: Let there be no <s>mokṣa</s> for one devoid of a widow!—thus declared the experienced libertines. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.29 //

children.text: raṇḍā vilokya taruṇaṃ karoti bhrukuṭiṃ mṛṣā /
children.translated_text: Seeing a young man, the widow frowns falsely,

children.text: kaṇṭhagrahaṃ cintayantī manasā tu prahṛṣyati // KNarm_3.30 //
children.translated_text: while contemplating an embrace, she inwardly rejoices. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.30 //
Remembering the pleasures of love, with plump thighs and breasts,

children.text: raṇḍā bhagasthalīṃ rātrau mṛdnātyucchvāsinī sadā // KNarm_3.31 //
children.translated_text: the widow at night always rubs her pubic region, sighing deeply. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.31 //
She gazes sidelong at a handsome young man, priding herself on her beauty,

children.text: sravantī nirbharaṃ reto raṇḍā dhenuḥ payo yathā // KNarm_3.32 //
children.translated_text: the widow secreting fluids copiously—like a cow giving milk. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.32 //

children.text: gauraḥ supīvaro dhatte raṇḍāyā muṇḍito bhagaḥ /
children.translated_text: The widow's shaved sex, fair and very plump, creates
the illusion of the golden slopes of <s>Meru</s> licked clean of grass by the horses of the Sun. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.33 //
A man procured from a horse-dealer, with a stiff, long staff—

children.text: yadi nāma rate śakto raṇḍāṃ toṣayituṃ na vā // KNarm_3.34 //
children.translated_text: whether or not he is able to satisfy the widow in love-making! // <s>KNarm</s> 3.34 //
At funeral feasts, the widow, a wave of passion, falls

children.text: vaśe patati dhanyānāṃ raṇḍā rasataraṅgiṇī // KNarm_3.35 //
children.translated_text: under the sway of fortunate, innocent Brahmins and matted-haired ascetics. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.35 //
With a flower placed in his topknot, a sacred thread over his ear,
a young Brahmin devoted to a widow is compared to <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love). // <s>KNarm</s> 3.36 //
To the fierce celibate student (<s>brahmacārin</s>) with an upraised great staff,

children.text: raṇḍā dadāti satataṃ śraddhayā mṛtabhojanam // KNarm_3.37 //
children.translated_text: the widow always faithfully gives funeral-feast food. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.37 //
She always takes him along on pilgrimages afterwards,
carrying an offering-tray and incense-box in a sword-shaped vessel. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.38 //
With mutually desired shaved sex and raised staff,
those two—the widow and the celibate—cause earthquakes at night. // <s>KNarm</s> 3.39 //
By day, salutations to the pilgrim who serves holy sites to preserve his hypocrisy;
by night, salutations to the celibate drunk from drinking at the widow's sex! // <s>KNarm</s> 3.40 //
The widow, out of deference to the matted-haired ascetics of <s>Gauḍa</s> and <s>Lāṭa</s>,

children.text: dadāti .. rjitāṃ prītyā talliptoru .. vāsakṛt // KNarm_3.41 //
children.translated_text: lovingly gives... [text damaged]... anointing the thighs... // <s>KNarm</s> 3.41 //

children.text: gatvā gurugṛhaṃ raṇḍā patyuḥ parvadine satī /
children.translated_text: Going to the <s>guru</s>'s house on her husband's ceremonial day, the faithful widow,

children.text: kaṣantī kaṭimā .. bhī raṇḍā nirdayamohanaiḥ // KNarm_3.42 //
children.translated_text: the widow rubbing her waist... [text damaged]... with merciless enchantments, // <s>KNarm</s> 3.42 //
The widow, who observes various vows such as funeral-rites and initiations for the deceased—

children.text: dadāti niśi niḥśaṅkā kāmasattraṃ tapasvinām // KNarm_3.43 //
children.translated_text: She fearlessly gives at night a festival of love to the ascetics. // 3.43 //
Under the pretext of worshipping the <s>liṅga</s>, having locked the house,
the widow satisfies her itch with a leather <s>liṅga</s>. // 3.44 //
Then, being attended to by that doe-eyed woman, the guru was agitated,

children.text: śiṣyāśca tāṃ papurnetraiḥ kṣudhārtāḥ kṣīriṇīmiva // KNarm_3.45 //
children.translated_text: and the disciples drank her in with their eyes, like hungry ones gazing at a milk-cow. // 3.45 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the widow.

children.translated_text: Then those men who had taken the vow of initiation entered,
blindfolded, as if blinded by false delusion. // 3.46 //
Then, with knees placed on the ground and hands folded in reverence, he informed
the guru—the market-ascetic whose inner sanctum was purified by faith—on behalf of the official. // 3.47 //

children.text: ihaiva suciraṃ nātha yāgavyagre tvayi sthite /
children.translated_text: 'O lord, while you have been occupied here for so long with the sacrifice,
other disciples are waiting, eager for the festive sacrifice.' // 3.48 //

children.text: ya eṣa prathito loke gṛhakṛtye mahattamaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He who is renowned in the world as the greatest in domestic affairs—
having begun the sacrifice, he awaits you.' // 3.49 //
'Whatever innumerable sins such as <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin) he has,
all were removed by you with merely a single stroke of the bell.' // 3.50 //
'He considers all sin, even universal destruction, as trivial as a blade of grass,

children.text: yato mūrdhni tvayā hastastasya pañcaphaṇo dhṛtaḥ // KNarm_3.51 //
children.translated_text: since you placed your five-hooded hand upon his head.' // 3.51 //
'By your grace, he has attained some exalted state,

children.text: śaṅkarāyatanebhyo 'pi śaivaḥ sarvaṃ jahāra yat // KNarm_3.52 //
children.translated_text: since, though a <s>Śaiva</s> devotee, he has robbed everything even from the temples of <s>Śaṅkara</s>.' // 3.52 //
'Seizing all possessions is a righteous good deed, the destruction of Brahmins—
all that is but the manifestation of your own teaching upon that man who is beyond doubt.' // 3.53 //
Thus ends the section on the 'greatest in domestic affairs,' or the self-serving one.
'O lord, this courtesan has come to invite you;
let a pot-installation ceremony be performed in her house, O lover of disciples.' // 3.54 //
'By the enchantment powders always bestowed by you,

children.text: asthiśeṣāḥ kṛtāste te yayā dhanikakāmukāḥ // KNarm_3.55 //
children.translated_text: those wealthy lovers have been reduced by her to nothing but bones.' // 3.55 //
'With oaths on cremation-ground treasures, her tongue, hands, and lips worn out,
she is protected only by your amulets, this one who moves in the guise of a lover.' // 3.56 //

children.text: tailonmṛṣṭe manāksneho vadane na tu cakṣuṣi /
children.translated_text: 'On her oil-anointed face there is slight affection, but not in her eyes;
a courtesan has no aversion toward the lowest castes among those whose wealth is depleted.' // 3.57 //
'If a courtesan were truly devoted, if Time were merciful,
if a <s>Kāyastha</s> (scribe) were not a thief—then a courtesan too would be a true lover.' // 3.58 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the courtesan.

children.translated_text: 'This eye-doctor has arrived—an ascetic and refuge of all,
by whose barley-wick eye-salves the entire world has been made blind.' // 3.59 //
'In summer, due to the abundance of eye diseases, when autumn fruits are at hand,
let a complete sacrifice be performed, with uninterrupted <s>pāṇḍuvallī</s> (white creeper) offerings.' // 3.60 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the eye-doctor.

children.translated_text: 'This barber-surgeon, who lives off men,
has swollen men's testicles to the size of large pots with his terrible plasters.' // 3.61 //
'He who previously installed <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s> for the sake of obtaining skulls—
that one desires a sacrifice by you on the rainy day for her sake.' // 3.62 //
'The wise one who, for a great price, for the purpose of nose-reattachment,
even cuts a piece of flesh and gives it from his own wife's body.' // 3.63 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the surgeon.

children.translated_text: 'And this old merchant with great wealth, married to a young woman,
desires aphrodisiacs due to his poverty of potency in lovemaking.' // 3.64 //
'How can a young wife enjoy herself with an old man who is pampered, with watery eyes,
wheezing and coughing, with a flaccid dangling member?' // 3.65 //
'Even when mounted for love, his flag destroyed by the effort of rising,

children.text: vṛddhaḥ prāpnoti no nidrāmṛṇaṃ dhyāyannivādhanaḥ // KNarm_3.66 //
children.translated_text: the old man gets no sleep, like a poor man brooding over debts.' // 3.66 //
'Though his member resembles a squeezed-out intestine, eager for love,

children.text: hastaṃ dattvā bhage vṛddho nidhānamiva rakṣati // KNarm_3.67 //
children.translated_text: the old man, placing his hand on the vulva, guards it like a treasure.' // 3.67 //
'Having eaten meat, milk, and ghee with hopes of love,

children.text: rātrau vamati tatsarvaṃ bhajate vā viṣūcikām // KNarm_3.68 //
children.translated_text: the old man vomits it all at night or gets cholera.' // 3.68 //
'Seeing her husband, resembling dried leather, for a moment at the nuptial reception,

children.text: sajane taruṇī dṛṣṭvā hrītā yāti rasātalam // KNarm_3.69 //
children.translated_text: the young wife, seeing him in public, sinks into the underworld with shame.' // 3.69 //
'By this old merchant, with medicines prescribed by aged rakes,
with his ointment-smeared member, the wife is constantly tormented as if burned.' // 3.70 //
'This very one, ever opportunistic in devouring large deposits,
a field for the drainage of wealth, the merchant is a daytime thief.' // 3.71 //
'The crooked serpent of the <s>Kali</s> age dances during times of disease,
selling unknown grasses, sticks, and such under the names of medicines.' // 3.72 //
'The old man, with unblinking eyes, gazes at his beloved who yearns for a young man—
he looks from afar like a sick man gazing at a fine meal.' // 3.73 //
'Therefore, procuring a flower-essence, let a ritual be performed with the power of <s>mantras</s>,

children.text: gṛhiṇī rāgiṇī yena labdhaśakteḥ prajāyate // KNarm_3.74 //
children.translated_text: by which his wife may become amorous when he has gained potency.' // 3.74 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the section on the old merchant.

children.translated_text: Having heard the invitations conveyed by such disciples,
the guru, with eyebrows raised in excitement, said, 'I shall do everything.' // 3.75 //
Then at day's end, having prepared a large fire-pot of <s>Śiva</s> in front,

children.text: guruṇā saha te śiṣyāḥ papurbhuktottaraṃ ciram // KNarm_3.76 //
children.translated_text: those disciples, together with the guru, drank long after eating. // 3.76 //
All the women of the officials, and their friends and relatives,
drank from skulls, vomiting it up and drinking again repeatedly. // 3.77 //
Then one began to sing, one weeps aloud,
one staggers about, one floats along making whistling sounds. // 3.78 //
One, feigning extreme disability born of devotion,
stands motionless for a long time as if he had attained the state of a corpse. // 3.79 //
One, adorned with swaying garlands, intoxicated with passion,

children.text: kṛtakaṇṭhagrahaḥ puṃsāṃ cucumba lalanā api // KNarm_3.80 //
children.translated_text: grasping throats, kissed men and women alike. // 3.80 //

children.text: tataḥ kṣībo guruḥ kiṃ citsvakāvyaṃ deśabhāṣayā /
children.translated_text: Then the drunken guru sang a little of his own poetry in the vernacular,
accompanied by the prominent sounds of <s>vīṇā</s>, flute, and strings, while playing the <s>kocchikā</s> instrument. // 3.81 //
Then, raising one arm in bliss with one hand,

children.text: gururnanarta dvābhyāṃ ca śanairutthāya cāsanāt // KNarm_3.82 //
children.translated_text: the guru danced, slowly rising from his seat with both feet. // 3.82 //
Then the disciples rose up, roaring with loud laughter,
embracing women, their waist-cloths slipping off. // 3.83 //
As midnight slowly passed and the circle of lamps went out,
their great festival of the circle of love became indiscriminate. // 3.84 //
At dawn, the guru arose and hastily distributed consecrated pots,
and performed everything as before, being invited by other disciples. // 3.85 //
For physicians, the time of fever is golden; for officials, the autumn season;

children.text: puṣpakāle gurūṇāṃ ca hemapūrṇā vasundharā // KNarm_3.86 //
children.translated_text: and for such gurus, the flower season—the earth is filled with gold. // 3.86 //
Then entered a man, breathing heavily, trembling as if about to burst,
looking sideways—a most trusted confidant of the official. // 3.87 //
He said, 'Today at midnight, the greatest in domestic affairs,

children.text: rājarāśidhanaṃ bhūri hṛtvā yātaḥ sahānugaḥ // KNarm_3.88 //
children.translated_text: having stolen a vast heap of royal wealth, has fled with his followers.' // 3.88 //
'When that one slipped away without telling anyone, among the officials connected to him

children.text: palāyanavyatikaraḥ ko 'pi jāto gṛhe gṛhe // KNarm_3.89 //
children.translated_text: there arose a scramble to flee in house after house.' // 3.89 //
'Your master, his face slapped open, has been taken to prison by soldiers;
his excrement falling as he walked—that former protector!' // 3.90 //
'Before your beard is plucked out and you too are bound and taken away,
let some strategy be devised in this terrible royal danger.' // 3.91 //

children.text: iti bruvāṇe tanmitre taiḥ śiṣyaiḥ sahite gurau /
children.translated_text: As his friend was speaking thus, the guru together with those disciples

children.text: tūrṇaṃ prayāte niḥśvasya niyogī duḥkhito 'vadat // KNarm_3.92 //
children.translated_text: quickly departed; the official, sighing in grief, said: // 3.92 //
'Alas! Due to the wickedness of Time, how terrible is this <s>Kali</s> age!

children.text: sādhavaḥ sarvathā naṣṭāḥ kaṣṭaṃ dharmo 'stamāgataḥ // KNarm_3.93 //
children.translated_text: Good people are utterly ruined; alas, <s>Dharma</s> has set!' // 3.93 //
